ActivityCategory.description:
Activity is an intentionally separate projection. Adding a field to the
security audit does not automatically expose that field in product feeds.

actor_role.description:
Stable role label captured at audit time. It is not re-derived from the
viewer's current role.

audit_id.description:
Stable audit identity. Replayed snapshots/events use this same value so
consumers can merge by identity instead of by UI presentation.

category.description:
Server-classified activity kind. UI clients must not infer this from
localized copy.

object_kind.description:
Stable typed object identity used for filtering and permission-checked
links. `resource` remains the immutable audit resource string.

reason.description: Stable reason/denial code, never arbitrary localized prose.

ApplicationIdentity.description:
A concrete application identity used by traffic rules. A display name is
deliberately not part of the identity: it is presentation-only and cannot
authorize or select a route.

CapabilityKind.description:
The fixed first-version capability set. Unknown wire values fail closed at
deserialization and are never inferred from a free-form label.

oneOf.description:
A migrated record may preserve an unreadable state without making the
capability usable. New writes may not create this state.

ConfirmedTrafficDirectFallback.description:
Explicit, acknowledged permission to fall back to the operating-system
route for a bounded set of failure classes. The policy is fail-closed unless
this value is present and valid.

ContentHash.description: SHA-256/Blake3-style content digest represented without exposing secret input.

ContributionKind.description:
Node-local contributions that the owner may veto independently of network
governance. Coordinator participation is deliberately not a local veto:
Coordinator terms are governed by the separate coordinator contract.

oneOf.description: Elected by a majority of the configured candidate group.
Temporary authority during partition. It cannot perform governance writes.

CoordinatorCandidate.description:
One administrator-selected Coordinator candidate. Lower priority values
are preferred, with node identity as the deterministic tie-breaker.

CoordinatorCandidateConfig.description:
Administrator-signed candidate group. Possessing this document is not
sufficient to become Leader: the signer must be a current network manager
when the document is admitted, every candidate must be a network member, and
election still requires the majority protocol defined by `CoordinatorTerm`.

CoordinatorCandidateDeclaration.description:
A short-lived, node-signed statement used as candidate health/eligibility
input. It is never a vote, majority proof or Leader promotion.

CoordinatorCandidateStatus.description:
Shared UI projection. `latest_term` is retained even after expiry so the UI
can show recent tenure without pretending the old leader still has authority.

eligible_for_election.description: Eligibility for the election protocol, never an appointment as Leader.

CoordinatorElectionVote.description:
A candidate-signed vote for one exact term and Leader. The signature binds
the network, candidate configuration revision, complete candidate group,
Leader and validity interval so a vote cannot be replayed for another term.

oneOf.description: No term has been admitted yet. Governance remains in bootstrap mode.
The lease is still writable, but renewal is overdue soon.
Authority is no longer writable until a fresh term is admitted.

CoordinatorLeaseStatus.description:
Observable lease projection used by the control plane and UI. `reason_code`
is stable so a clock-skew alert cannot be mistaken for an ordinary expiry.

CoordinatorPublicReachability.description:
Public reachability evidence supplied by the candidate itself. Consumers
must treat this as a claim until the election protocol verifies a quorum.

DomainName.description:
Canonical, case-insensitive DNS name used for exact host matching. IDNs are
normalized to their ASCII A-label form and a single trailing root dot is
accepted but not retained.

EffectiveAccessReason.description:
Stable explanation of the final effect. UI surfaces consume this
projection instead of re-implementing rule precedence.

ExitContributionAvailability.description:
Availability projected beside a member's declared capability. Unknown or
stale evidence is never promoted to `available`.

ExitContributionMemberScope.description:
Owner-selected members that may use this node's Exit. The default allows all
active network members; an explicit selection requires at least one subject.

ExitContributionMode.description:
Explicit Exit contribution policy. The legacy obligation/scope pair remains
on the wire for compatibility, but it cannot distinguish voluntary
contribution from a prohibition or an authorization flow. New policies bind
this mode into terms hashes and signed discovery data.

oneOf.description: Members may explicitly opt in; joining never enables Exit locally.
The member must provide Exit capacity as a condition of joining.
Members may not contribute Exit capacity to this network.
Members may request authorization before contributing Exit capacity.

ExitContributionObligation.description:
Exit contribution is an explicit network admission obligation, not a
capability silently enabled by joining.

ExitContributionRestrictions.description:
Owner-authored restrictions beyond the global network allow-list and local
Exit veto. The network allow-list remains `NodeLocalAccessPolicy::network_scope`.

ExitContributionScope.description:
The membership population covered by an Exit contribution obligation.
`NotApplicable` is the only valid scope when contribution is not required.

oneOf.description:
New members accept the obligation when they join. Existing members are
notified but retain their previously acknowledged scope.

Every member must acknowledge the current obligation. This is used for
a policy migration that expands contribution to the existing roster.

ExitContributionTimeWindow.description: UTC half-open minute window. `weekdays` uses Monday=0 through Sunday=6.

ExitNodeCapabilities.description:
Current, non-secret Exit Node capability truth for one node process.

`supported` describes whether a basic IPv4 Exit Node can be installed now.
`ipv6_forwarding` is independent because an IPv6-only limitation does not
make the IPv4 Exit Node implementation unusable.

ExitNodePlatform.description: Host platforms with distinct Exit Node implementation requirements.

ExitNodeUnsupportedReason.description:
Machine-readable reasons that make an Exit Node action unavailable.

Adapters must render these reasons instead of treating an enabled config
flag as proof that kernel forwarding and NAT were installed.

ExitSelectionCandidate.description:
Stable reason code and scope for one Exit. Unknown and stale availability is
never reported as selectable.

ExitSelectionGroupRule.description:
An administrator-defined group scope. Membership is part of this policy so
an Exit decision never depends on a client-supplied or stale role label.

ExitSelectionMemberRule.description: A member-specific narrowing or deny. A deny always wins over every allow.

ExitSelectionMode.description:
Schemars cannot infer the human-readable shape from the hand-written serde
implementation above. Keep the JSON contract as the original internally
tagged representation while Postcard uses its own positional-safe form.

ExitSelectionPolicy.description:
Versioned administrator policy. `available_exits` is the network-level
allow set and therefore the universe of all other scopes. Group `allow`
lists narrow that universe when the subject belongs to a matching group;
member `allow` lists narrow it further. Any matching deny removes an Exit
regardless of allow rules at any scope.

ExitSelectionResolution.description:
Complete administrator-authorized set for one subject. Candidate ordering is
stable to make UI and audit output reproducible.

ExitSelectionSource.description: Where the final decision came from.

ExitSessionTransitionPolicy.description:
What to do with an already established session when its Exit is no longer
selectable. `Migrate` may still fail closed if no replacement is available.

FieldPrivacyPolicy.description:
Immutable network-authored field policy. Revisions are monotonic and carry
both issuance and effective time. A malformed, duplicate, expired or
not-yet-effective policy fails closed.

FieldVisibility.description:
Audience ceiling for one field.

The ordering is from least to most restrictive. `serde` aliases preserve
compatibility with the pre-W10 three-level node privacy documents.

FieldVisibilityRule.description: One explicit field override. A policy can only tighten the supplied floor.

IpCidr.description:
IP/CIDR matcher stored as text at the contract edge for cross-language
portability and parsed before policy activation.

LocalExitCapabilitySnapshot.description: Owner intent and observed lifecycle of the local Exit data plane.

MembershipRole.description:
A member's governance role. Temporary Coordinator authority is intentionally
represented by `CoordinatorTerm`, never by mutating this durable role.

MembershipState.description: The durable state of one node's relationship with one network.

exit_contribution_mode.description:
Explicit four-mode policy. Omitted from the canonical hash for legacy
Required/JoiningMembers and NotRequired/NotApplicable records so their
acknowledgements and signatures remain verifiable.

member_limit.description:
Capacity shown when these terms were acknowledged. Omitted for legacy
memberships so their content hash remains stable.

NetworkAcl.description:
Revisioned network ACL. Explicit deny rules live in `rules`; direct
role/group/node grants live in `grants` and are subject to expiry,
revocation and reauthentication freshness.

relay_limits.description:
Administrator-authored hard resource bounds for using Relay. Provider
local limits are intersected with these values.

NetworkAclGrant.description:
One explicit direct grant. Grants are additive allow entries; they never
override a matching deny in either authorization layer.

NetworkDiscoveryDocument.description:
Signed discovery data. Endpoints may change between revisions; the stable
network ID remains bound to the immutable network public key.

administrators.description:
Public governance roles disclosed before joining. Full member IDs,
endpoints beyond the signed public hints, topology and activity remain
outside this document.

capability_summary.description:
Canonical capability declaration summary. This is discoverability
metadata, not proof that a capability is currently operational.

language.description:
Public discovery facets. Schema v2 includes these fields in the signed
payload. Defaults keep older local JSON readable while validation still
rejects records created under a different document schema.

publisher.description:
Node that published this revision. Schema v1 binds the publisher to the
network owner so another member cannot publish an owner-authorized card.

revoked_at_unix_ms.description:
A signed tombstone is a normal revision with this timestamp set. Once a
client accepts one, every older or non-identical successor is rejected.

NetworkEndpoint.description: A decoupled discovery hint. It is never part of the stable network identity.

NetworkJoinMode.description: Admission policy selected by the network owner.

oneOf.description: Requests are accepted immediately.
Requests enter `pending_approval`.
The node must first consume a signed, single-use invitation.

NetworkMemberObservationSource.description:
Why presence has its current value. The timestamp lets both UIs display the
observation's freshness without inventing a client-side observation.

NetworkMemberOnlineState.description:
Three-state presence. Unknown means the Coordinator has never observed the
member's data-plane session and must never be presented as offline.

NetworkMemberStatus.description:
Authoritative, sanitized member status shown by governance surfaces.

This is deliberately distinct from [`MembershipState`], which tracks the
local node's connection workflow. In particular, an approved roster member
is not reported as active until a live data-plane session observes it.

oneOf.description: 仅使用 IPv4 虚拟内网
仅使用 IPv6 虚拟内网
同时支持 IPv4 和 IPv6 虚拟双栈

NetworkRole.description: Durable network roles plus the runtime-only emergency Coordinator role.

NetworkVisibility.description: How much of a network's public profile is discoverable without membership.

NodeAccessControlSnapshot.description:
Trusted authorization documents carried with the authoritative node state.
`local_policy` is authored by the node owner; each network ACL is authored by
that network's governance. Duplicate network ACLs are never resolved by
ordering and cause command authorization to fail closed.

field_privacy_policies.description:
Versioned network-authored field disclosure documents. Like ACLs,
these are trusted control-plane data and never come from command JSON.

NodeCapabilityRegistrySnapshot.description:
Stable projection of the fixed first-version capability set. Unknown
entries fail closed and unsupported capabilities remain visible so the UI
can explain why an action is unavailable.

NodeConfigurationSnapshot.description: Effective, non-secret network configuration exposed to every UI adapter.

NodeContributionVeto.description: A non-overridable local contribution veto for one network.

NodeControlHealth.description: Whether the adapter can currently reach the node control plane.

NodeDiscoveryIndexErrorCategory.description: Stable, non-secret categories for persisted request failures.

NodeDiscoveryIndexMetrics.description:
Aggregate-only discovery telemetry. It deliberately has no URL, response
body, search text, record name or free-form error text.

NodeDiscoveryIndexSnapshot.description: Public discovery-index status included in the canonical node snapshot.

data_plane_affected.description:
The discovery index is a control-plane convenience. Its state never
changes any joined network's lifecycle or forwarding data plane.

search_history_stored.description:
The discovery index client has no search-query field. This explicit flag
documents the privacy contract for generated UI and Android clients.

NodeDiscoveryIndexSource.description:
One signed record accepted from the index or supplied by a join flow.

`discoverable` is false for expired, malformed or revoked records. The raw
signed record is retained so revocations and revision watermarks survive a
restart and can reject later rollback attempts.

NodeDiscoveryIndexState.description: Stable discovery-index states consumed by every UI adapter.

NodeEmbeddedServiceSnapshot.description:
Non-secret runtime state for one network's embedded signaling and relay
services. Invitation tickets, identity material, and host-local paths are
deliberately excluded from this shared UI contract.

coordinator_candidates.description:
Administrator-signed candidate group, verified declarations and the
currently authoritative leader/term projection. Missing means the
runtime has not supplied candidate status yet; it is never inferred.

relay_authorization.description:
Owner-visible, bounded explanation of the current Relay authorization
decision. It excludes matching rules, grants and transport metadata.

relay_health.description:
Authoritative Relay health from the node runtime. Missing means no
health evidence is available; adapters must not infer health from the
listener address or lifecycle status.

relay_status.description:
Relay is an independently owned capability; it can be stopped while the
embedded Coordinator keeps running.

NodeErrorCategory.description:
Stable error domains shared by command results, HTTP responses and
WebSocket failures. UI code must branch on this category rather than parse
human-readable messages.

NodeExitSelectionSnapshot.description:
One network's administrator-owned Exit selection policy plus the exact
deny-first resolution produced by the trusted runtime. Older snapshots omit
this field and therefore must not infer an authorized Exit.

NodeIdentitySnapshot.description: Public node identity metadata. Secret key material must never enter this DTO.

created_at_unix_ms.description:
Unix timestamp when the current identity key was created. This remains
optional so snapshots produced by older nodes can still be decoded.

NodeInterfaceOwnership.description:
Product ownership is established by an exact match against the live
runtime's TUN name. Interface naming conventions never establish ownership.

NodeInterfaceSnapshot.description:
One redacted host network interface captured by the node process.

The snapshot intentionally omits hardware addresses, routes, policy rules
and operating-system diagnostics. UI adapters render this projection and
never query or mutate host networking themselves.

NodeLifecycleSnapshot.description: Shared lifecycle snapshot consumed by CLI, IPC, WebUI, and (later) GPUI.

NodeLocalAccessPolicy.description:
The trusted, owner-authored local authorization layer. A network
administrator can add further restrictions but can never replace this
document or any of its vetoes.

exit_contribution.description: Owner restrictions specific to serving as an Exit for a network.

relay_limits.description:
Owner-authored hard resource bounds for serving Relay on this node.
Network ACL limits are intersected with these values; this document can
make them stricter but cannot loosen network-authored bounds.

NodeNetworkConfigSnapshot.description:
One network's effective configuration after loading startup overrides.

Filesystem paths and other host-local details are deliberately omitted. The
boolean fields only state whether optional host-local settings are present.

NodeNetworkMembershipSnapshot.description:
Public, owner-editable network metadata rendered by every UI adapter.

This is deliberately a separate projection from `NetworkRecord`: secrets,
members, addresses, topology, activity and invitations are not fields and
therefore cannot be serialized by accident.

current_terms.description:
Signed terms most recently observed from discovery. When these differ
from `terms_hash`, members see a policy-change notice; the separate
boolean distinguishes notice-only metadata changes from Exit disclosure
or privacy changes that require explicit acknowledgement.

NodeNetworkRole.description: Network roles are capabilities within a network, never product identities.

NodeNetworkScope.description:
A node owner can either participate in every authenticated network or
explicitly limit participation to a fixed set. An empty `Only` set is
invalid rather than an accidental allow-all sentinel.

NodeNetworkSnapshot.description: One local network and the roles this node currently performs in it.

NodePeerSnapshot.description: Peer state scoped to a network. The same node may appear in multiple networks.

NodePermission.description: Stable capability classes used by both the permission snapshot and UI actions.

NodePermissionSnapshot.description:
Control-plane authorization posture shared with UI adapters.

`TrustedControlPlane` means the runtime accepts every connected adapter as
fully privileged. It does not mean per-user or remote authentication exists.

NodePhase.description:
Node-global lifecycle. Network sessions may come and go while the node
remains in one of these phases.

NodeProblem.description: UI- and transport-neutral error returned by every node command adapter.

oneOf.description:
A finite host resource (memory, file descriptors, storage or firewall
capacity) prevented the requested operation.
The operation is valid but unavailable on this platform or host.

NodeProblemDetails.description:
Stable machine-readable error details. Human-readable messages remain in
`NodeProblem::message`, while these fields are safe for adapters to use for
field highlighting and revision conflict recovery.

NodeRoutingDefaultAction.description:
The default action currently applied to traffic that does not match a
network-specific rule.

NodeRoutingSummarySnapshot.description:
One network's authoritative traffic-policy state as last applied by the
node runtime. Editable configuration remains in `NodeConfigurationSnapshot`.

oneOf.description: Runtime accepted the policy and the matching snapshot was published.

The last successful application predates the current stopped/runtime
state and must not be treated as active.
Policy validation rejected the configuration before mutation.
The runtime or snapshot publication failed after an application attempt.

NodeRoutingTargetSnapshot.description: Concrete traffic path behind a network or Exit default action.

NodeValidationIssue.description: Structured field-level validation issue carried by a command error.

PrivacyField.description:
Stable field identifiers. Serialized policies and public previews use these
names verbatim; hidden values are never represented by a masked placeholder.

PublicKey.description: Ed25519 public key bytes encoded as URL-safe base64 without padding.

RelayAuthorizationAuditSnapshot.description:
Bounded, deterministic snapshot of current Relay member decisions. The
owner sees which authorization layer produced the final result without the
matching rule/grant identifiers or any connection metadata.

truncated.description: True when the policy contained more members than the bounded projection.

RelayAuthorizationSourceDiagnostic.description:
Sanitized authorization evidence for the Relay owner. It deliberately omits
rule and grant identifiers, matched subjects and transport metadata while
retaining the layer, reason and revisions needed to explain both sides of
the final decision.

RelayExistingSessionPolicy.description: How existing sessions react when Relay authorization changes.

oneOf.description: Keep the already-established encrypted QUIC session until it closes.

Move the member to another authorized Relay without dropping its P2P
overlay session.
Close the relayed session promptly and fail closed.

RelayGovernanceAction.description: Stable governance action names for audit records and activity filters.

RelayGovernanceAuditSnapshot.description:
Snapshot returned by the Relay governance sink. Older events are evicted
first; `dropped_events` makes queue pressure observable rather than silent.

RelayGovernanceEvent.description:
One bounded, payload-free Relay governance observation.

Events intentionally carry no source/destination address, peer display
name, packet payload, key material or session secret. `node_id` identifies
the consumer whose request was rejected or whose authorization changed so
an owner can filter the audit without exposing the Relay topology.

policy_revision.description: Policy revision that became effective for this governance event.

previous_policy_revision.description: Policy revision observed before an authorization or quota update.

RelayHealthSnapshot.description:
Health is derived from observed state. It cannot be set to healthy by a UI
merely because an owner intent or capability declaration is present.

RelayLimitPolicy.description:
Hard limit set for one Relay direction. When a network policy and a node
policy both define a value, [`RelayLimitPolicy::intersection`] keeps the
stricter one.

RelayUsageSnapshot.description:
Measured Relay work. This is a projection, not an accounting journal; the
authoritative audit remains the append-only audit chain.

Signature.description: Signature bytes encoded as URL-safe base64 without padding.

TopologyBoundary.description:
One network boundary. `member_count` is the authoritative count, while
`visible_member_count` reflects aggregation so a surface can explain it.

TopologyCluster.description: Aggregated remainder of an oversized network.

TopologyConnection.description: One unordered node pair, with every network that observed it.

TopologyConnectionState.description:
Link state as observed, not as assumed. `Stale` is terminal for rendering
purposes: it never counts as an active link.

TopologyNode.description: Exactly one entry per `NodeId`, regardless of how many networks it joins.

networks.description: Sorted by network id so both UIs render the same order.

TopologyNodeHealth.description:
Aggregated node health. `Unknown` is deliberately distinct from `Healthy`
so a surface can never claim a healthy node it has not observed.

TopologyNodeNetwork.description: The node's relationship with one visible network.

TrafficAction.description:
Exactly one traffic decision. Network and Exit decisions carry the concrete
target in the variant, so a rule can never return an ambiguous set of exits.

TrafficDefaultConfirmedBy.description:
Who explicitly confirmed the fallback decision for traffic that matches no
rule. There is intentionally no default confirmation value.

TrafficFailureKind.description: A condition that prevents the selected route from being used.

oneOf.description: Process identity could not be established for an application condition.
DNS resolution did not produce an answer before the deadline.
DNS answers failed authenticity/consistency checks and may be poisoned.
The selected network or concrete Exit is no longer available.
No authorized network path could be selected.
A connection did not establish before the policy deadline.

The secure handshake with a Relay or Exit was interrupted after it
started. Existing flows may have observed partial authentication state,
so this class must fail closed.

The local runtime lost ownership of or disconnected from the data-plane
process. It cannot prove that traffic remained inside the protected
path, so this class must fail closed.

Some attempts completed and others failed, so switching routes would be
ambiguous or could leak an already-established flow.

direct_fallback.description: Absence is the fail-closed default and is not shown as confirmation.

destination_cidrs.description:
Exact IP values are canonicalized as `/32` or `/128`; CIDRs are matched
only against the observed destination IP.

domain_suffixes.description:
Complete-label DNS suffix match, for example `example.com` also matches
`www.example.com` but never `notexample.com` or `example.com.evil`.

exact_domains.description:
Exact, normalized DNS names. This condition never parses or compares IP
literals and never matches a subdomain.

TrafficMatchRisk.description:
A non-blocking warning attached to a matcher. Invalid or ambiguous values
are rejected by `validate`; these codes describe valid rules whose scope is
intentionally or accidentally broad and must be shown before activation.

TrafficProtectionState.description: What the runtime can prove about the local traffic path right now.

oneOf.description: No protected route has been selected yet.
A route is being established and has not completed validation.

An existing route is being replaced and traffic is fail-closed until
the replacement completes validation.
Fresh TUN, route, DNS and reachability evidence all passed.
Traffic must be stopped because the selected route cannot be trusted.

The owner/administrator explicitly allowed this exact failure class to
use the operating-system route.

TrafficRoutingHardConstraints.description:
Hard routing constraints shown alongside the policy. They are not editable
policy rules and must never be bypassed by direct fallback.

TrafficRoutingMoveAction.description:
One equivalent pointer/keyboard/button action. Adapters bind drag-and-drop
and keyboard gestures to the same action ID rather than implementing a
second ordering path.

TrafficRoutingObservation.description:
A bounded observation window produced by the real traffic data plane. Only
samples that the runtime actually observed are present here; adapters must
never synthesize hits from tests, fixtures or configuration.

observed_flow_count.description:
Total observed flows in the window, including flows outside the
bounded sample list.

TrafficRoutingObservedHit.description:
One real observed flow that matched the rule. `activity_id` or
`diagnostic_id` provides the stable one-click source for the tester.

authority_revision.description: Applied authority revision, not a local form counter.

can_edit.description:
Whether the current caller may create a draft or apply it. Read-only
callers still receive the authoritative page and target navigation.

observation.description:
Observation availability is part of the authoritative page so the UI
can distinguish an observed zero-hit window from missing data.

TrafficRoutingRuleActivityEffect.description:
The observable consequence of disabling or deleting a rule. `NoObservedTraffic`
means an available observation window confirmed zero matching flows; it is
never used when the observation source is unavailable.

delete_impact.description: Authoritative consequence of deleting this rule.

disable_impact.description:
Authoritative consequence of disabling this rule. The default keeps old
snapshots honest: absence of observation data is unavailable, not zero
hits.

TrafficRoutingTarget.description:
A navigable reference to a routing target. Labels are display hints; stable
IDs and `navigation` are the authority used by every adapter.

TrafficRoutingWorkflowState.description:
The editor workflow state. `Draft`, `Applying`, `Applied`, `Failed` and
`Stale` are intentionally separate so an adapter cannot infer success from
an editable document or from the mere presence of a revision.

oneOf.description: No authoritative traffic policy has been loaded yet.

TrafficSessionEvent.description:
A compact, transport-neutral activity record. It contains stable state and
reason codes only; Exit identities, addresses, resolver URLs and command
output stay outside this projection.

TrafficSessionSnapshot.description: The single source of truth consumed by GPUI, WebUI and protocol adapters.

TrafficSessionValidation.description: Evidence required before the session may become `Protected`.

TunCapabilities.description:
Redacted TUN readiness for the current node process. This is deliberately
derived from capability metadata rather than a real TUN creation probe.

UiMode.description:
The actual control surface selected for this node process.

`WebUi` is the browser-hosted control plane for headless hosts. A process
with a desktop session must use `Gpui`; it must not expose the WebUI as a
second desktop surface.

description: Stable, transport-neutral state rendered by every node UI adapter.

access_control.description:
Trusted node-owner restrictions and versioned network governance ACLs.
Authorization consumes these documents directly; UI capability hints
are never used as policy input.

capabilities.description:
Unified four-capability projection shared by every UI adapter. Missing
entries deserialize as `Unknown`; they are never inferred as enabled.

control_health.description:
Health of the UI adapter's control connection. This is local transport
observation, not authoritative node state, so changing it must not
manufacture a new node revision.

discovery_index.description:
Signed public discovery-index projection. This control-plane state is
isolated from joined network lifecycle and forwarding data planes.

exit_node_capabilities.description:
Runtime capability truth for this host. Adapters must disable Exit Node
actions when `supported` is false and render the typed reasons instead
of inferring success from configuration alone.

exit_selections.description:
Authoritative administrator Exit-selection evidence for each cached
roster. The resolution is computed by the same deny-first engine used by
runtime admission; adapters must render it rather than re-resolving the
policy locally. Missing entries from older nodes deserialize as empty.

interface_problems.description:
Redacted problems encountered while collecting or reconciling host
interfaces. Command and runtime failures remain in `last_error` when
they are tied to a network lifecycle transition.

interfaces.description:
Authoritative host interface capture for the node page. This is filled
by the node process from OS network state; UI adapters never probe the
host themselves. Missing data deserializes as an empty capture.

local_exit.description:
Authoritative local Exit lifecycle. `owner_exit_enabled` is the durable
local veto; network Exit roles only decide whether the data plane may
serve after this intent is true.

memberships.description:
Durable local membership acknowledgements, one per stable network ID.
This projection contains no private keys, peer addresses or topology.

network_profiles.description:
Owner-authored public network-profile projections. This field is an
allowlisted public snapshot: it never contains member identities,
addresses, topology, activity, invitation tickets or secret material.

recent_activity.description:
Up to 256 recent user-meaningful command outcomes. Entries are already
redacted by the domain audit projection and ordered newest first, so
every UI adapter consumes the same short-term activity feed.

routing_summaries.description:
Authoritative per-network traffic-policy summaries. The node runtime is
the only writer; UI adapters never derive "applied" state from editable
configuration. Missing data from older peers deserializes as empty.

topology.description:
Privacy-filtered topology derived from the cached roster plus live peer
sessions. `None` means the node has no identity yet, so no graph can be
drawn at all; a present but empty snapshot means nothing is joined.
Adapters never project membership themselves.

traffic_routing_page.description:
The single authoritative traffic-routing editor projection. The node
runtime builds this from the applied policy, hard constraints and
current caller permissions; adapters never reconstruct it from legacy
network configuration. Missing data means the production policy/TUN
adapter is unavailable, not that an empty policy was applied.

tun_capabilities.description:
Redacted TUN readiness for this node process. Missing or malformed
capability data must disable host-network mutations in every adapter.

title: NodeSnapshot
